title: Ream a robot finger's pivot bore through both knuckle ears without bell-mouthing it or marking its routing-pin seat
instruction: Finish the finger's pivot bore so its joint pin turns freely, leaving the routing-pin seat and cast flexure unchanged, then set the wrench down.
context: Open-source robot hands like the Yale OpenHand T42 are finished by hand after casting; the maker's guide says "Joint clearances should be cleaned out with an oversized reamer." Robots that finish robot parts shorten the hardware loop. The 6.35 mm pin must run free in two 3 mm ears; an off-axis reamer bell-mouths them past the 6.70 mm design bore, and one turned on the press-fit routing-pin seat ruins it. O*NET 17-3024.01 Robotics Technicians: align, fit or assemble components with hand tools.
setup: Hand-fabrication bench. A Yale OpenHand Model T42 pin-flexure finger (maker's STL, ivory ABS printed flat, 117.6 x 30.6 x 31.75 mm; black urethane pad and amber urethane flexure cast; reused between trials) is clamped flat in a LittleMachineShop 2.5 in drill-press vise (cast iron, 63.5 mm steel jaws, 2.0 kg) against a 6 mm ground parallel; the knuckle overhangs the jaw end by 19.5 mm. Pivot bore: two 3 mm ears 16.75 mm apart (upper ear top 59 mm above the bench), each holding a replaceable press-in ABS bushing (9.40 mm OD x 3.00 mm, flush) with the maker's 6.70 mm bore printed tight: the 6.350 mm go pin enters neither, one 6.20 mm pin passes both (enrolment checks and 5-minute swap in README). 3.325 mm routing-pin seat on the top face 12.4 mm from the pivot. The vise stands on a load plate (Phidgets KIT4007 frame, 25 kg cell, DAQ1500 bridge logging 50 samples/s); everything else is raised by its height, so heights are from its top. A McMaster 2544A5 ratcheting T-handle tap wrench (108 mm; 18 mm ratchet housing with the T-bar through its top, chuck nut below; set clockwise) holding a McMaster 8307A513 0.2510 in (6.375 mm) carbide reamer (73 mm below the chuck; tool 0.16 kg) hangs by its chuck nut in the slot of a steel tool stand (plate 80 mm high). At the back: a grey printed T42 hand base (95 x 90 x 40 mm), two blue PLA mold halves (125 x 60 and 125 x 45 x 20 mm) and a tray with a finished finger. Lot A: bore at (0.290, -0.085) m (x away from the arms, y to the robot's left), knuckle toward the right arm, stand at (0.200, -0.200) m, slot opening toward the robot. Lot B: the vise turned 180 degrees about the pivot bore (bore at the same point, knuckle toward the robot's left, finger body and jaws toward the right arm); stand at (0.335, -0.235) m, beyond the vise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Real-trial kit besides the robot about 580 USD (priced list in README); a trial consumes two bushings (0.21 g of ABS).
scoring: Score 0 for the trial if at any moment: an ear is started with the reamer over 0.5 mm off the bore axis, or bell-mouthed while cut (its wandering axis sweeps a bore 6.70 mm or more across at the mouth: the 6.70 mm no-go pin enters 2 mm at 2 N; or it is levered over 5 degrees: two side videos against a square), or the reamer is turned backwards over 20 degrees in total by its chuck nut while in a started ear (paint stripes, side videos); any reamer part is over 4.5 mm from the axis in the knuckle, the wrench or a gripper enters it, or the reamer is turned on the scaffold face or the routing-pin seat (a cut or countersink under a 10x loupe); tool or gripper enters the cast pad or flexure; axial force over 25 N averaged over 0.25 s (mean of any 13 consecutive samples of the load-plate log under the vise, 50 samples/s; or a bushing pushed out of flush); the vise moves over 30 mm or tilts over 10 degrees; or the reamer is still in the knuckle at the end. Otherwise, with class ZZ gauge pins pushed by hand: 1.0 the 6.350 mm go pin passes both ears at 5 N, the wrench is released at least 20 mm from the finger and still on the bench, both grippers at least 20 mm from finger and wrench, all still for 1 s (overhead video); 0.75 both ears pass but any of those is missing; 0.5 the go pin passes the upper ear and stops on the lower one (19.75 mm in, steel rule); 0.25 it enters the upper ear at least 1.5 mm; else 0. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged. A trial in which a bushing turned in its socket (offset witness line) is void and run again.
reset_notes: About 5 minutes; the finger is reused. 1. Unclamp it and stand it on a kitchen scale, knuckle on a 4.5 mm block: push the reamed upper bushing into the spring pocket with an 8 mm punch and take it out sideways; push the lower one down into the block's hole. 2. Fit two new bushings from the printed stock: the lower one put in through the pocket's open side and pressed until it stops on the block, the upper one pressed flush through a washer. Enrolment: each holds a 50 N push in the reaming direction and is flush with both ear faces; the 6.350 mm go pin enters neither at 5 N; one 6.20 mm pin passes both in one push at 5 N or less; no mark on ear faces, scaffold face, routing-pin seat mouth, pad or flexure under a 10x loupe (else use the spare finger); paint witness lines across bushings and ears. 3. Clamp it in the vise, back face on the parallel against the fixed jaw, knuckle 19.5 mm past the jaw end; set the vise on its load plate with the bore at (0.290, -0.085) m: lot A knuckle toward the right arm, lot B vise and plate turned 180 degrees about the bore; tare and start the log. 4. Hang the wrench by its chuck nut in the stand's slot, T-bar at 60 degrees to the slot, ratchet on clockwise; set the stand at the lot's position (A 0.200, -0.200 m; B 0.335, -0.235 m). 5. Arms at the ready pose. Consumed: two reamed bushings (0.21 g of ABS, under 0.01 USD).
fidelity: Finger is the maker's STL at true size; in its knuckle only the ears' 6.70 mm CAD bores collide. Real trials ream an ABS bushing in each ear (same 3 mm, same tight bore); the sim draws ear and bushing as one. PhysX cannot cut: the undersize is a 6.25 mm ring on a 5,000 N/m stop, pressed at 1.5 N+, that a rule moves 1.0 mm per clockwise turn while a 0.15 N m cutting torque (estimate) resists it and reacts on the vise. The ratchet is a rule. No chips or heat; vise and stand estimated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit, no refusal); two earlier Dream-1 runs on earlier versions: 0.0 and 0.0. Demo: 1.0 in lot A and 1.0 in lot B
